searchText: Alternatively, something like Curve4Q might be fast for you? Go implementation: https://github.com/cloudflare/circl writeup: https://bifurcation.github.io/fourq/ It's based on 2^127-1 extension field which should be decently fast. Or alternative 2, use a Curve on an extension like https://github.com/pornin/ecgfp5 which uses Goldilocks (2^64 - 2^32 + 1) base field with extension of degree 5. bonus: it's cheap to prove in Plonky2 / Goldilocks based proof systems For what is worth, Ukrainian digital identity is using binary curves: https://github.com/ikripaka/dstu4145-rust/pull/1 Thanks yeah alternative 2 will lead to better bandwidth, do you know how these two curves compare ? (Speed of MSM) you still use extension fields so you send 5x 64 bits for EcGfp5 basically small base field --> extension fields needed to grow the number of bits now there might be way to store points in a compressed form but I don't know enough of this curve for it. Curve4Q has a 4 dimensional endomorphism, I expect the speedup is similar to BLS G2 with/without endomorphism. Goldilocks can be implemented without carries on a 64-bit CPU meaning it's extension field benefits maximally from instruction-level parallelism (4 independent additions in 1 CPU cycle on Intel CPUs, 6 on Apple Silicon). All to say, i have absolutely no idea. Thanks. At this stage it seems the larger risk is patents and the fact that Vitalik didn't like it, but will benchmark with some curves when shadow is available 4 dimensional endomorphisms make a nice speedup on BLS G2, like 1.8x or so If it's substantially faster than reed Solomon it may be worth it patents on?
